title: coord.py serve: the same commands over HTTP for several operators, standard library only
goal: coord.py serve --bind [HOST:]PORT --keys DIR runs an http.server front end over the SQLite store that answers each coord.py command as a JSON request, and coord.py --url URL --key-file PATH sends any command to it instead of a local store, so agents on other hosts share one service; wait is a long-poll; each operator has a token of its own, read from its own file (on the server one file per operator in DIR, named for the operator, so removing it revokes that operator), and the server refuses a request whose token is unknown or revoked with 401 and names the operator on each event it records; the token check is one authentication function, so an OAuth2 bearer-token check can replace or join it later; the server binds to 127.0.0.1 unless --bind names a host, port 0 picks a free port, the first line it prints names its URL, and keeps no secret in argv or the environment of a child process.

run:
import os,subprocess as s,sys,tempfile,time
T="_tools/coord.py"
if not os.path.isfile(T):print("coord.py missing: the work adds it");sys.exit(1)
d=tempfile.mkdtemp();keys=os.path.join(d,"operators");os.mkdir(keys);sec="k"*40
open(os.path.join(keys,"alice"),"w").write(sec);open(os.path.join(d,"alice.key"),"w").write(sec);open(os.path.join(d,"mallory.key"),"w").write("m"*40)
E=dict(os.environ,KB_COORD_STORE=os.path.join(d,"coord.sqlite"))
srv=s.Popen([sys.executable,T,"serve","--bind","0","--keys",keys],stdout=s.PIPE,stderr=s.STDOUT,text=True,env=E)
try:
    url=srv.stdout.readline().split()[-1].strip()
    def c(key,*a):
        p=s.run([sys.executable,T,"--url",url,"--key-file",os.path.join(d,key),*a],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=60,env=dict(os.environ));return p.returncode,p.stdout+p.stderr
    r=c("alice.key","claim","k1","--ttl","60");u=c("mallory.key","claim","k2","--ttl","60")
    c("alice.key","post","--kind","heartbeat","--field","item=ST-aaaaaaaa");w=c("alice.key","wait","--since","0","--timeout","2")
    argv=s.run(["ps","-o","args=","-p",str(srv.pid)],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
    os.remove(os.path.join(keys,"alice"));rv=c("alice.key","claim","k3","--ttl","60")
    res=dict(loopback=url.startswith("http://127.0.0.1:"),claim=r[0]==0,unknown_401=u[0]!=0 and "401" in u[1],event_names_operator="alice" in w[1],
     no_secret_in_argv=sec not in argv,revoked_401=rv[0]!=0 and "401" in rv[1])
finally:
    srv.terminate();srv.wait(10)
print(res);sys.exit(0 if all(res.values()) else 1)

gates.question: How does coord.py serve authenticate agents of several operators?
options: one shared token read from a file with mode 0600, sent in a request header
one token per operator, each read from its own file, so a token can be revoked alone
gates.recommendation: one token per operator, each read from its own file, so a token can be revoked alone
gates.answer: one token per operator, each read from its own file, so a token can be revoked alone; the token check sits behind one authentication function so an OAuth2 bearer-token check can replace or join it later
